card: Adds a functional test to verify that P2P address messages with out-of-range timestamps are clamped to five days in the past. Currently, net_processing logic handling addresses too far in the future or too far in the past lacks explicit test coverage. The author demonstrates that the test kills two mutants in net_processing.cpp that disable either check.
changed_since_previous: No changes to the patch content; diff is now available.
evidence: The PR description demonstrates that the test kills two mutation test mutants in PeerManagerImpl::ProcessAddrs in net_processing.cpp where each condition check is replaced with false.
problem: P2P address processing in net_processing clamps timestamps that are too far in the future (over 10 minutes) or too old (at or below 100,000,000s) to five days in the past, but this clamping behavior lacked functional test coverage.

risk.why: Only touches functional test code; a failure would cause CI flakiness rather than affecting node runtime.

summary: Adds a functional test to verify that peer address messages with out-of-range timestamps are clamped to five days in the past. It sends addresses with timestamps far in the future and far in the past to an inbound peer and verifies their stored times in addrman.
